disease_label_per_paper: Disseminated skeletal coccidioidomycosis with cutaneous draining clavicular lesion
presentation_summary: 44-year-old African-American man with no known medical history presented with three months of painful lumps over the left clavicle and scapula.
The clavicular lesion had burst open and drained pus for several days.
He denied fever, weight loss, appetite change, or bone pains; examination was afebrile with stable vital signs.
Chest x-ray was clear, but radiographs, CT, and bone scan showed pathologic clavicle fracture and multiple expansile lytic lesions in clavicles, scapula, vertebrae, ribs, pelvis, and sacrum.
Bone biopsy showed necrotic granulomatous tissue with Coccidioides spherules and culture/PCR confirmed Coccidioides immitis; MRSA also grew from the lesion.
After further questioning he reported spending two weeks in Arizona a few months earlier.

quality_warnings: Biopsy, culture, and PCR are confirmatory and marked use_in_ranking false.
The case has strong skeletal/cutaneous presentation but no active pulmonary imaging abnormality at presentation; pulmonary absence is preserved instead of deleted.
No numeric serum labs were reported in the case text aside from negative diagnostic workup categories, so none are fabricated.
